title: 1993 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Which of the following sets could NOT be the lengths of the external diagonals of a right rectangular prism [a “box”]? (An external diagonal is a diagonal of one of the rectangular faces of the box.)

solutions.text: If the edge lengths are \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) then the three face-diagonal squares are \(a^2+b^2,\) \(a^2+c^2,\) \(b^2+c^2.\) For sorted diagonals \(p\le q\le r,\) \[ a^2=\frac{p^2+q^2-r^2}{2}, \] so necessarily \(r^2\lt p^2+q^2;\) the analogous formulas show this is also sufficient. Only \(\{4,5,7\}\) fails, since \(7^2=49\gt16+25=41.\) Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: If \(p\le q\le r\) are the face diagonals, express the edge squares in terms of \(p^2,q^2,r^2\)
A necessary and sufficient positivity condition is \(r^2\lt p^2+q^2\)
